parsed.explanation: The dossier documents a current morality-law regime used to criminalise gender nonconformity and transition, with up to five years’ imprisonment and no anti-discrimination recourse. That is a trans-specific, visitor-facing exposure if outed, not merely a dead-letter sexuality statute. Missing domestic gender recognition is given limited weight, though the text explicitly leaves mismatched visitor documents unreconcilable. Religious rulings narrowing perceived legitimacy add climate and care-related suspicion. Violence evidence is severe but dated and located in militia-controlled areas; incomplete reporting prevents treating executions/torture as a nationwide present campaign, yet documented militia targeting of effeminate or accused gay people is organised, high-severity risk in those subnational regimes. No state execution or routine arrest pattern is proven, so it sits above the 0.05 anchors, but criminalisation plus lethal subnational targeting and no effective remedy keeps it near the severe-risk boundary. Uncertainty is high; absent evidence of relief implies unresolved risk.
